item.title: 1. Select jobs, not tests
item.description:
Date: 2026-11-13. Status: accepted.

Context

Picking tests is already well served: CircleCI Smarter Testing, and the test impact tools from several other vendors. What nobody covers well on CircleCI is which jobs and workflows a change needs, together with their order, approvals, filters and contexts.

Decision

Smarter Workflows decides at the level of jobs and workflows. Inside a job it runs, test selection is left to Smarter Testing or to whatever tool the job already uses.

Consequences

  • The two layers compose: Smarter Workflows skips whole jobs, and Smarter Testing trims the tests inside the jobs that run.
  • The unit of everything here (impact map, plan, report) is a workflow job, never a test.

item.description:
Measured results for v0.3 on real CircleCI pipelines (2026-11-17). Older v0.1 tables remain for comparison.

v0.3 savings

From scripts/e2e/run-scenarios.sh on main at fdbdeac and the first scheduled learn runs. Method and caveats: Validation.

Target Projected savings Recall

Method

End to end — scripts/e2e/run-scenarios.sh pushes a one-commit branch per scenario, waits for the setup workflow and the continued workflow, and compares the jobs that ran with the expected set. Each scenario runs three times on the same base commit; medians use the per-target full-run scenarios as the baseline. Details: Validation.

Backtest — circleci-smarter backtest replays a JSON history file in select mode with a fixed impact map. Details: Backtest.

Performance — Go testing.B benchmarks and scripts/bench/perf.sh on generated configs and temporary git repos. Details: Performance benchmarks.

End-to-end savings

Job seconds are the sum of each job’s reported run time in the continued workflow (including smarter-gate). They are a stand-in for compute time, not credits: resource class affects credits, and queue time is excluded. On the demo monorepo, the two worker-test matrix jobs always run in v0.1, so they appear in every row below.

item.title: CircleCI workflow composer
item.description:
You wire jobs that already exist into workflows. You do not write jobs, steps or orbs. Load the CircleCI MCP skill write-config first (get_skill with skill: "write-config", then reference: "references/orbs.md"): it covers orbs, functions and validate_config. This skill adds only the workflow layer.

Tags such as cfg#requires name the source of a rule; the URLs are at the end. (heuristic) marks advice that is not a documented rule.

Inputs

  • The job inventory, circleci-smarter catalog --config .circleci/continue.yml: the only source of job names, kinds, parameters, workspace use, contexts and filters.
  • The guardrail settings, the constants at the top of policies/guardrails.rego: mandatory jobs, restricted contexts, resource classes.
  • Optional: job durations from green default-branch runs (references/tools.md §3).

Workflow

  1. Read the catalog. For each selected job note its kind (build, approval, no-op, release), what it persists or attaches, its contexts and filters, matrix or parameters, orb or local. Copy names exactly. Mark the mandatory jobs and every job that uses a restricted context. If a job you need is not listed, stop and report it.
  2. Decide the stages. Everything runs in parallel unless an edge has a reason: a data contract (a consumer attaches what a producer persists), fail fast (cheap before expensive), policy (a restricted context needs an approval), order of effect (deploy after every check), shared state (serial-group). Usual order: cheap checks and the mandatory scan as roots, build, expensive checks, gate, approval, deploy, cleanup and notify.
  3. Wire requires. Fan out from producers. Collapse N×M with a no-op coordinator. Require a matrix by its alias and a job group by its name. Use a status other than success only on cleanup, notify and rollback jobs.
  4. Add conditions. Filters, workflow when, step when. Give an approval and the jobs behind it the same filters.
  5. Add the gate. One type: no-op job named smarter-gate, with no filters, that requires every check job and nothing behind the approval. It is the single required status check.
  6. Check the whole file, in this order: circleci config validate FILE, circleci-smarter layout check ..., circleci-smarter policy check ... (commands: references/tools.md §4 and §5).
  7. Repair. Read each finding’s code and message (references/tools.md §4 maps a finding to a fix), fix the cause in the layout, and run all three checks again. If a finding survives three repairs, stop and report it. Never pass a check by weakening the layout: do not drop a mandatory job, an approval, a context restriction or a branch filter, and do not edit policies/.
  8. Report the layout in a few lines, the result of each check, and what you could not verify. Leave everything outside the workflow you compose (other workflows, jobs, orbs, comments) as it was.

Hard rules

Layout

  • Add no job except approvals, no-op coordinators and the gate. Use catalog names verbatim. One entry per job, or distinct name: values. cfg#name
  • Write only keys that the references or the docs list. A misspelled key on a local job fails to compile; on an orb job it can be ignored without a word (write-config skill).
  • Every requires item is an entry of the same workflow: its name:, a matrix alias or a job-group name. No cycle. The compiler rejects the rest. cfg#requires cfg#matrix-requires
  • A required job that does not run is ignored, and a job whose requirements are all filtered out does not run either. Work this out for every filtered job and every approval. cfg#requires
  • Statuses are success, failed, canceled, unauthorized, not_run and terminal. A job that requires X: failed or X: terminal gets the filters of X: the docs do not say what happens when X is filtered out. (heuristic) cfg#requires

Approvals, contexts, mandatory jobs

  • An approval is type: approval on a workflow entry, with a unique name and no steps. Every job after it requires it. Place it after all checks, directly before the first job that must not run unapproved. wf#approval
  • An approval and every job behind it carry the same filters. Filter only the approval and the job runs unapproved; filter only the job and the workflow waits on hold. cfg#requires wf#approval
  • Keep the contexts the catalog gives a job and add none it does not need; with several, later ones win. ctx#combine
  • A restricted context goes only on the jobs the bundle lists, behind an approval, with filters.branches.only in map form. Keep such jobs out of job groups. ctx#approve (policies/guardrails.rego)
  • Mandatory jobs are plain entries (not in a job group), unfiltered, with no requires unless they need another job’s output, so no earlier failure keeps them from running. cfg#requires (policies/guardrails.rego)

Gate

  • The gate is type: no-op with no filters. It requires every check job, directly or through coordinators, and nothing behind the approval, nor any cleanup or notify job. At least one of its requirements always runs. cook#gate cfg#requires

Data

  • A job that attaches a workspace is downstream of every job it needs data from. Concurrent producers persist disjoint paths. A cache never carries this run’s output between jobs. ws#overview cache#race

Conditions

  • Conditions read pipeline values and parameters, never environment variables. Never put << >> inside a bare expression. A when step takes a logic statement, not an expression. cfg#logic cook#when

Speed and cost

  • Put the quickest jobs first, and add an edge only for a reason: a needless edge lengthens the critical path. wf#examples support#workflow-review
  • Use serial-group for deploys and other shared state, and max_auto_reruns only for jobs known to be flaky. cfg#serial-group rerun#wf

Planner v0.1

  • Prefer what the planner can evaluate: map branch and tag filters, and requires by success. A matrix, an expression filter, a non-literal workflow when or another status makes it run more, or leaves a job out of the gate. (docs/spec/v0.1.md steps 1, 5, 6; docs/limitations.md)

Which reference to read

When you Read
wire requires, use a status, filter a job or an approval, use a matrix or a job group references/requires-and-statuses.md
shape the graph: fan-out, coordinator, gate, fail fast, critical path, approval, deploy, serial-group, reruns references/shaping-patterns.md
write when, unless, filters or step conditions references/conditions.md
fix an order because of workspaces, caches or artifacts references/data-flow.md
call a tool or read a finding references/tools.md
want a complete, valid layout to copy examples/

Examples, each validated with circleci config validate: 01-small.yml (parallel checks, one build, a gate); 02-medium-fanout-workspaces.yml (workspaces, fan-out, a matrix by alias); 03-deploy-gated.yml (approval, restricted context, serial-group, cleanup, notify, gate).

Tools

Need Use
Job inventory circleci-smarter catalog --config F [--map M] [--workflow W]
Layout findings circleci-smarter layout check --config F [--catalog C] [--policy-bundle D] [--mandatory LIST] [--restricted-contexts LIST]
Guardrails circleci-smarter policy check --config F --bundle policies --format json
Compile circleci config validate F, or MCP validate_config (pass org for private or URL orbs)
What CircleCI documents docs MCP search_circle_ci_knowledge_sources: one complete, generic sentence
Job durations MCP list_runs, list_run_workflows, list_workflow_jobs (started_at, ended_at)
Flaky jobs MCP list_flaky_tests
Orb job parameters MCP get_orb_source, before you use an orb job

catalog and layout check are built alongside this skill: if --help differs from references/tools.md, --help wins. Never print environment variables or secrets.

item.title: Contributing
item.description:
Thank you for helping to improve Smarter Workflows, a CircleCI Labs project. Field engineers review issues and pull requests on a best-effort basis, with no SLA. Report a security problem by email, not in an issue (SECURITY.md).

Reporting a bug

Search the existing issues first, and check that you use the latest release or main. Then open a new issue. Include:

  • The planner version (circleci-smarter version, or the orb version) and the mode you ran in (shadow or select).
  • The plan.md and plan.json that the plan job stores as the artifacts smarter-plan/. They list every job, whether it ran, and why.
  • The files that the change touched, what the plan did, and what you expected.
  • The part of your continue.yml that shows the problem, reduced to the few jobs that matter.

Remove tokens, internal host names and private code from everything you paste.

Requesting a feature

Open an issue. Describe the problem, and name the command, the flag or the file it affects. For problems in the CircleCI platform, contact CircleCI support instead.

Opening a pull request

Before you open a pull request:

  1. Discuss large changes in an issue first.
  2. Run the checks of Development.
  3. Update docs/ when you change a flag, a file format or a default.
  4. Write every commit message, and the pull request title, as a Conventional Commit (Commit messages).
  5. Check that the diff has no tokens, host names, or customer or vendor names. The repository is public.
  6. Add a dependency only when its release is at least 7 days old, and pin it exactly: in go.mod, and by version and checksum for a tool that CI downloads.

A pull request that changes only documentation (docs/, site/, Markdown files) runs the docs site build and skips the jobs that do not read those files. That is the planner at work: this repository plans its own pipeline (How it works).

Commit messages

Use Conventional Commits: type(scope): summary. Keep each commit small and atomic.

Type Use for
feat A new capability, or a changed command, flag or file format
fix A bug fix
docs Documentation only
test Tests only
ci The CircleCI pipeline
chore Maintenance with no user-visible change
refactor, perf Code changes that keep behavior, or improve speed

A breaking change adds ! after the type or scope (feat(plan)!: rename a flag), or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer that says what the user has to change.

Development

Requirements: Go (the version in go.mod), and the CircleCI CLI, which the tests use to validate every config that the planner generates. Config validation needs a CircleCI API token (circleci auth login locally, or the smarter-workflows-ci context with CIRCLE_TOKEN in CI on this project). Set REQUIRE_CIRCLECI_CLI=1 to make a missing CLI or token fail the tests instead of skipping them.

gofmt -l .
go vet ./...
go test ./...
circleci policy test policies

The commands check formatting (the output must be empty), vet, the Go tests, and the Rego tests of the guardrail bundle. Restricted contexts in policies/guardrails.rego are deploy, smarter-workflows-release, and smarter-workflows-ci (API token for config validation on go-test and orb-validate). CI also runs shellcheck -s sh scripts/*.sh. The golden files of the example monorepo change with go test ./examples/monorepo -update: read the diff before you commit it.

Validation lists every test layer, and .circleci/continue.yml is the pipeline that runs them.

Keep the repository generic: no customer, vendor-specific or internal names, host names or links. Never print environment variables or secrets in a script, a test or a log.

Documentation

Documentation follows the CircleCI docs style: sentence-case headings, active voice, no contractions, and short sentences. Every docs/*.md page has front matter with page-title, page-audience, and page-description.

Documentation site

The documentation is also a site on GitHub Pages: https://circleci-labs.github.io/smarter-workflows/. CircleCI builds it with Hugo and the Hextra theme, and pushes it to the gh-pages branch. The Markdown stays the only source, and nothing in it is written for the site: README.md is the home page, and site/nav.txt lists the other pages (docs/, the glossary, the composer skill, the compose eval, the demo, this file and the security policy).

Add every new, renamed or removed page to site/nav.txt. site/stage.sh fails on a Markdown file below docs/ that the list misses, and on a listed file that does not exist, so docs-site-build catches a page that would be missing from the sidebar. STAGE_LENIENT=1 turns both errors into warnings while you restructure. A relative link to a file that is a page of the site goes to that page, and a link to any other file of the repository goes to GitHub.

To preview the site, install Hugo extended 0.168.0 and Go (Hugo downloads the theme as a Go module), then run from the repository root:

site/stage.sh
cd site && hugo server --bind 127.0.0.1 --baseURL http://127.0.0.1:1313/

Run site/stage.sh again after you change a page. To run the check of the pipeline, install lychee and run (cd site && hugo --minify --panicOnWarning) && site/check.sh. It checks every link and heading anchor of the built site, offline.

The job docs-site-build runs this check on every branch. It reads only the docs and the site sources, so the planner skips it for a change that touches neither. The job docs-site-publish runs on main only, in the workflow docs-site, and pushes the site to gh-pages with the context smarter-workflows-release. Hugo and lychee are pinned by version and SHA-256 in the command docs-site of .circleci/continue.yml: a new version needs its new checksum, from the release page of the tool, in the same change.

A maintainer does this once:

  1. Put a fine-grained token for this repository only, with the repository permission Contents: read and write and nothing else, in the variable GITHUB_TOKEN of the context smarter-workflows-release. Without the variable the job builds and checks the site and publishes nothing.

  2. Restrict the context to this project, and refuse SSH reruns:

    circleci context restriction create smarter-workflows-release --org <ORG> --type project --value <PROJECT_ID>
circleci context restriction create smarter-workflows-release --org <ORG> --type expression \
 --value 'not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")'

  3. After the first publication, open Settings, Pages, and set Source to Deploy from a branch, the branch to gh-pages and the folder to / (root). GitHub then deploys every push to that branch. There is no workflow file to maintain.

License

By contributing, you agree that your contributions are licensed under the MIT license.

item.title: Quickstart
item.description:
Note

CircleCI Labs project, 0.x, not supported by CircleCI support. What is tested and Limitations describe current coverage.

Adoption path

  1. Trial learn locally with a read-only CircleCI token or a recorded history file (circleci-smarter learn --history FILE --learned-out …). Read the report’s recall and incomplete jobs.
  2. Add the orb with plan on every pipeline (shadow) and learn on a schedule. Attach a context with CIRCLECI_TOKEN and optional ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
  3. Switch to select when shadow plan.md and the weekly learn report agree.

Schedule trigger

  • GitHub App projects: Project Settings → Triggers → Schedule → add a weekly trigger on the default branch.
  • OAuth projects: use scheduled pipelines (pipeline parameter or trigger type schedule).

The orb example wires learn to pipeline.trigger.type == "schedule" and keeps plan on other triggers (shadow-learn-schedule.yml).

Setup config (orb) 

version: 2.1
setup: true
orbs:
 smarter: cci-labs/smarter-workflows@0.3.0
workflows:
 plan:
 when:
 not:
 equal: [schedule, << pipeline.trigger.type >>]
 jobs:
 - smarter/plan:
 config: .circleci/continue.yml
 workflow: ci
 mode: shadow
 mandatory: security-scan
 policy-bundle: policies
 ai-review: shadow
 executor: smarter/go
 source: build
 resource_class: medium
 refresh-learned:
 when:
 equal: [schedule, << pipeline.trigger.type >>]
 jobs:
 - smarter/learn:
 config: .circleci/continue.yml
 workflow: ci
 limit: 200
 context: [your-circleci-token-context]
 executor: smarter/go
 source: build
 resource_class: medium

Until the orb is published, copy the inline jobs from this repository’s .circleci/config.yml (they build the planner from source).

Catalog

  1. Move jobs, workflows, orbs and executors to .circleci/continue.yml. That file is the catalog; nothing Smarter-specific is required inside it.
  2. Turn on setup workflows under Project Settings → Advanced.

Analyze treats mapped inputs as directory prefixes (. is the whole repo). Jobs with opaque steps always run until learn improves the map.

Artifacts and branch protection

  • Every plan run stores smarter-plan/plan.md, plan.json, and analyze-report.md.
  • Every learn run stores smarter-learn/learn.md and learn.json, and updates the learned layer cache (learned-key-prefix, default smarter-learned-v1).
  • Require the continued workflow’s GitHub check, or per-job smarter-gate if you use job checks.

Pipeline parameters

If continue.yml uses workflow when/unless on pipeline.parameters.*, set the parameters job parameter to a JSON file of values. The planner writes parameters.json under the plan report for continue.

Optional guardrails

Copy policies/, edit settings at the top of guardrails.rego, and set policy-bundle: policies on plan. Run circleci policy test policies.

Several pipelines in one project

Share one project cache but give each setup config its own learned-key-prefix. No prefix may be a prefix of another (use smarter-demo-learned-v1 beside smarter-learned-v1, not smarter-learned-v1-demo).

item.title: Spec v0.1
item.description:
Status: building. Decisions: docs/adr/. Words: Glossary.

Goal

A setup workflow runs the circleci-smarter planner. For a branch, the planner prunes the planned workflow of .circleci/continue.yml down to the jobs the change can reach. It checks the result against the guardrails and continues the pipeline. From v0.3 the impact map comes from circleci-smarter analyze (ADR 8); the trace-based map build described below is historical v0.1 behaviour.

Not in v0.1

  • History mining and learned rules.
  • Model deciders (LLMs or hosted decision models).
  • Compose mode.
  • Signing the map.
  • Multi-workflow pruning (other workflows pass through with the same meaning).
  • Matrix expansion (matrix entries always run).
  • Looking inside a job group (an entry that names one always runs, as one unit).
  • Expression filters (they are reported and left out of the gate).
  • Chunk sidecar integration.

Layout 

cmd/circleci-smarter/ main.go (dispatch) + one file per command, each registering itself in init()
internal/config/ parse, prune, inject and emit CircleCI YAML (yaml.Node, so order and comments are kept)
internal/diff/ base resolution (merge-base), changed files
internal/impactmap/ map format, trace TSV parsing, `map build`
internal/planner/ the selection algorithm, plan, the gate and the trace/map job injection; the layout check
internal/catalog/ the catalog JSON of a workflow (`catalog`)
internal/pipelineparams/ JSON pipeline parameter files for plan and continue
internal/report/ plan.json and plan.md
internal/analyze/ static impact-map inference (v0.3, separate command)
internal/policy/ local evaluation with circle-policy-agent; repair codes
internal/continuation/ POST /api/v2/pipeline/continue
policies/ the Rego guardrail bundle + tests
orb/src/ orb-tools layout: commands install, collect-trace; job plan; scripts/
.circleci/ config.yml (setup, dogfood) + continue.yml (this repo's full pipeline)
examples/monorepo/ an example continue.yml, impact map and scenarios with golden plans

CLI contract (circleci-smarter <command>)

Exit codes for all commands:

  • 0: ok;
  • 1: fatal error;
  • 2: usage error;
  • 3: the guardrails failed and the pipeline must not continue (plan, policy check), or the layout has errors (layout check).

base

Prints the diff base SHA for the current checkout, or prints nothing (exit 0) when the branch gets a full run.

  • Flags: --default-branch (default main) and --branch (default $CIRCLE_BRANCH).
  • The base is git merge-base origin/<default> HEAD. Run git fetch origin <default> first when origin/<default> is missing.
  • On the default branch, on a tag ($CIRCLE_TAG), or on any git failure, print nothing.

plan

Flag Default Meaning
--config .circleci/continue.yml the full continuation config (the catalog)
--workflow the only workflow the workflow to plan; an error if the config has several and none is named
--map /tmp/smarter/impact-map.json.gz the impact map (v2 gzip, or legacy v1 JSON at impact-map.json); a missing or invalid map means a full run
--base computed as base does the diff base
--head HEAD
--branch, --tag $CIRCLE_BRANCH, $CIRCLE_TAG
--default-branch main
--trigger-type empty schedule means a full run
--mode shadow shadow or select
--mandatory empty comma-separated job names
--full-run-paths .circleci/** comma-separated globs (doublestar); any match means a full run
--extra-inputs empty declared inputs, job=glob|glob,job2=glob
--ignore-paths empty globs that never select a job (they still count for --full-run-paths)
--force-full false
--trace auto auto, on or off; auto means on for full runs on the default branch
--trace-orb-jobs false also trace orb jobs (assumes their executor is Linux)
--trace-jobs (empty) comma-separated job-name globs: trace Linux jobs whose executor cannot be read (for example self-hosted runners); never traces Windows or macOS
--gate-job smarter-gate the name of the gate job, which is a no-op job (step 6)
--map-image a pinned cimg/base:<yyyy.mm> the docker image of the smarter-impact-map job (step 8). The gate has no image
--gate-image the same deprecated alias of --map-image: the flag used to set the image of the gate and the map job, and it still sets the map job’s. It prints a warning
--map-key-prefix smarter-impact-v1 the start of the cache key the map job saves the impact map under, <prefix>-<checksum of the commit>; letters, digits, ., _ and -. Pipelines of one project share its cache, so give each its own, and restore with the same prefix. Restore keys match by prefix: no prefix may start with another one plus a dash
--policy-bundle empty run the pre-flight and repair loop (ADR 6)
--policy-meta built from env JSON passed as data.meta
--out /tmp/smarter/continue.yml
--report-dir /tmp/smarter/plan
--parameters empty pipeline parameter values, as a JSON object: used to evaluate workflow when/unless and written to <report-dir>/parameters.json for continue

The head commit message forces a full run when it contains [smarter full] (case-insensitive) or a Smarter-Full: true trailer.

After a usable config is loaded, an internal error never fails the command. The planner writes a full plan instead, records the reason, and exits 0. That full plan still carries the gate job (and, on the default branch, the trace steps). Only a config that the planner cannot add the gate to (the gate’s name is taken, or two jobs share a name) is passed through as it came, without the gate, with a warning.

map build 

circleci-smarter map build --traces DIR --revision SHA --out PATH

Merges every *.tsv in DIR into one map.

policy check 

circleci-smarter policy check --config PATH --bundle DIR [--meta PATH] [--format text|json]

Exit codes: 0 means pass or soft-fail only; 3 means a hard violation.

catalog 

circleci-smarter catalog [--config PATH] [--workflow NAME] [--map PATH]

Prints, as JSON, the jobs of one workflow: what an agent needs to compose a workflow from them.

Flag Default Meaning
--config .circleci/continue.yml the continuation config
--workflow the only workflow an error (exit 2) if the config has several and none is named
--map none an impact map. Without one, no job has inputs. A map that is missing only warns; one that cannot be read is an error

Exit codes: 0 for a catalog, 1 for an error, 2 for a usage error.

{"version":1,"workflow":"ci","map_revision":"<sha or empty>",
 "jobs":[{"name":"api-test","ref":"api-test","kind":"build",
 "executor":{"type":"docker","image":"cimg/go:1.26","resource_class":""},
 "contexts":[],"filters":{},"requires":[{"job":"lint","status":["success"]}],"required_by":["hold-deploy"],
 "workspace":{"persists":[],"attaches":false},"serial_group":"","matrix":null,
 "inputs":{"traced":true,"complete":true,"files":8,"dirs":2,"top_dirs":[".","libs/shared","services/api"]},
 "steps":["checkout","run: Test the API"]}],
 "job_groups":[{"name":"rollout","jobs":["deploy","verify"]}]}

examples/monorepo/catalog.json is a full sample (a golden file of the tests).

  • One entry per job of the workflow (jobs), sorted by name, which is the entry’s name: if set, else its job. ref is the job it runs.
  • kind is one of:
    • build: a job that runs steps;
    • approval: type: approval, on the entry or in the job’s definition;
    • no-op: type: no-op in the definition;
    • release: type: release in the definition;
    • orb: a job the config does not define;
    • matrix: an entry with a matrix, whatever it runs;
    • job-group: an entry that names a group of the top-level job-groups.
  • executor is docker, machine, macos, windows or unknown, with the image (xcode:<version> for macOS) and the resource class as written. An executor named by executor: is looked up. Approvals, no-op jobs and release jobs have no executor, so they say unknown.
  • requires (sorted by job) has the statuses of each requirement: ["success"] for a bare name. required_by names the entries that require this one.
  • filters are the entry’s branches and tags filters as written, or {"expression":true} for an expression. {} means none.
  • workspace: persists lists the paths of the job’s persist_to_workspace steps, and attaches says whether it has an attach_workspace step. Steps in a local command, and in the entry’s own pre-steps and post-steps, count. Both are null when the steps are not visible.
  • serial_group is the entry’s serial-group as written ("" if none). matrix is null, or {"alias":"","parameters":{"os":["linux","mac"]}}.
  • inputs is what the impact map knows: traced is true when the job has an entry, complete and the counts are its. top_dirs are the directories of the files it read, two path segments deep (. is the root), or one when that gives more than 12; at most 12, sorted.
  • steps names each step in order: checkout, run: <name or first line, up to 80 characters>, or the step’s key. An orb job is ["unknown"], with an unknown executor and null workspace, unless the orb is defined inline in the config. So is a job group. An approval, a no-op job and a release job have no steps ([]).
  • job_groups lists the groups of the config, sorted, with the names of the jobs inside each.
  • The output is deterministic: lists that mean a set are sorted, and nothing depends on the order of the workflow or of the YAML maps.

layout check 

circleci-smarter layout check [--config PATH] [--workflow NAME] [--catalog FILE]
[--policy-bundle DIR] [--mandatory LIST] [--restricted-contexts LIST]
[--gate-job NAME] [--format json|text]

Checks the layout of one workflow, the way its jobs wait for each other, before it runs. It reads the workflow with the planner’s own graph, and plans nothing.

Flag Default Meaning
--config .circleci/continue.yml the config to check
--workflow the only workflow an error (exit 2) if the config has several and none is named
--catalog none what catalog printed. For a job that the config does not define (a layout may name the jobs of another file), it says what the job is and what it does with workspaces
--policy-bundle none also evaluate the guardrail bundle on the config: each violation is a finding
--mandatory none comma-separated jobs that the workflow must hold
--restricted-contexts none comma-separated contexts that only a job downstream of an approval may use
--gate-job smarter-gate the gate job. An empty value skips the gate checks
--format json json or text

Exit codes: 0 when there are no errors (warnings are fine), 3 when there are errors, 1 when the check itself fails (the config or the bundle cannot be read), 2 for a usage error.

{"version":1,"workflow":"ci","ok":false,
 "findings":[{"code":"dangling-requires","severity":"error","job":"deploy",
 "message":"deploy requires lintt, which no job of workflow ci answers to",
 "fix_hint":"add a job called lintt to the workflow, or remove it from the requires of deploy"}]}

job is the entry to edit (the missing job, for mandatory-missing and gate-missing; the first job to add, for a policy repair). The findings are sorted: errors first, then by code, then by place in the workflow.

Code Severity Fires when
dangling-requires error a requires names no entry of the workflow (an << expression >> cannot be judged). The hint says when the name is a job inside a job group, or the job of an entry that has a name:
cycle error entries wait for each other, or one requires itself
consumer-before-producer error a job attaches a workspace, and none of the jobs it requires, directly or not, persists one. A job whose steps are not visible (an orb job, a job group) counts as a producer and is never reported
restricted-context-without-approval error an entry that is not an approval uses a --restricted-contexts context, and has no approval among its ancestors
mandatory-missing error a --mandatory job is not in the workflow (by its name there)
gate-missing error no entry is called --gate-job
gate-not-noop error the gate’s job is not defined with type: no-op
gate-missing-requirement error a job that will run is not an ancestor of the gate. Not counted: approvals and no-op jobs, jobs downstream of an approval, jobs that require a status other than success, jobs that come after the gate, and the planner’s smarter-impact-map
gate-awaits-status-job error the gate, or a job it awaits, requires a job status other than success: it may never run, and the gate would wait for it for ever
filtered-approval-footgun warning a job requires an approval and at least one other job, and on some branch or tag the approval’s filters (or those of what it requires) leave the approval out while the job still runs. CircleCI ignores a requirement on a job that does not run, so the job runs without the approval. Filters are tried on every name they spell out, on a name that each regular expression matches, and on one name that no filter has
policy:<rule> error or warning the guardrail bundle reports the rule: error for a hard violation, warning for a soft one. The message is the bundle’s
duplicate-name error two entries answer to one name, so a requires cannot say which it means

A job group is one unit here: the check does not look inside it, so a restricted context used by a job inside a group is not seen.

continue 

circleci-smarter continue --config PATH [--parameters PATH]
  • Reads CIRCLE_CONTINUATION_KEY, and CIRCLECI_API_HOST (default https://circleci.com).
  • POSTs to /api/v2/pipeline/continue.
  • Retries on 429 and 5xx: 3 tries, waiting 1, 2 then 4 s.
  • Never prints the key or the request body. It prints only the status code.

version

Prints the version: dev-<sha> when built from source, otherwise the release tag.

File formats

Trace TSV

Superseded by ADR 8. v0.3 does not use trace TSV. This section documents the removed v0.1 collector format.

The collector writes one file per job node: <traces-dir>/<first 16 hex of sha256(job name)>.<node index>.tsv.

# smarter-trace v1
job <workflow job name, i.e. $CIRCLE_JOB>
node <$CIRCLE_NODE_INDEX or 0>
method atime
supported true|false
reason <why unsupported, optional>
F <repo-relative path of a git-tracked file that was read>
D <repo-relative directory that was listed; "." is the root>

Impact map

v2 (written by map build): gzip-compressed JSON at impact-map.json.gz.

{"version":2,"revision":"<sha>","created_at":"<RFC3339>","method":"atime",
 "files":["a/b.go","a/c.go"],"dirs":[".","a"],
 "jobs":{"<job name>":{"file_idx":"<base64 delta-varint indices>","dir_idx":"...",
 "complete":true,"nodes":2}}}
  • files and dirs are the sorted, deduplicated path tables for the whole map.
  • Each job’s file_idx / dir_idx is base64-encoded sorted delta-varints into those tables.
  • complete is true only if every node was supported.

v1 (legacy cache): uncompressed JSON with per-job path lists:

{"version":1,"revision":"<sha>","created_at":"<RFC3339>","method":"atime",
 "jobs":{"<job name>":{"files":["a/b.go"],"dirs":["a"],"complete":true,"nodes":2}}}

Readers accept both; writers emit v2 only.

Plan report

plan.json:

{"version":1,"mode":"select","full":false,"full_reason":"","workflow_runs":true,"workflow_skip_reason":"","workflow":"ci",
 "base":"<sha>","head":"<sha>","branch":"x","map_revision":"<sha>","map_created_at":"...",
 "changed":[{"path":"a/b.go","status":"M"}],
 "jobs":[{"name":"api-test","run":true,"reasons":["reads services/api/main.go"]}],
 "gate":{"name":"smarter-gate","requires":["..."]},
 "guardrails":{"status":"PASS","repairs":[],"violations":[]},
 "warnings":[]}

plan.md is a human summary for the job’s artifacts and (later) a PR comment:

  • one line: the mode, N of M jobs running, and the full-run reason if there is one;
  • a table of jobs, with run or skip and the first reason;
  • up to 50 changed files.

The algorithm (planned workflow W)

The planner first loads the config. It expands every YAML alias and merge key into an independent copy and drops the anchors, so that no edit below can reach a node that another part of the config shares. The emitted YAML means what the input meant; its formatting (indentation, anchors) may differ.

What an entry runs

The planner reads what each entry of W runs from the job’s definition (jobs: of the config), and from the top-level job-groups:

Kind Written as Selected by
job a job that runs steps (type: build, the default) its inputs (step 3), or the closure (step 4)
approval type: approval on the entry, or in the job’s definition the closure only
no-op type: no-op in the job’s definition: no executor, no steps, no credits the closure. One that no entry requires is a gatekeeper, and is always kept (step 7)
release type: release in the job’s definition (plan_name): it tracks the release that a deploy job planned any job it requires being selected (step 4)
job group the name of a group under the top-level job-groups, used as a job nothing: it always runs, as one unit (step 3)
orb job a job that the config does not define its inputs; no map entry means it runs

An approval, a no-op job and a release job run no steps, so they are never traced and have no inputs. A job group is not looked into: v0.1 plans it as one opaque unit. A serial-group key of an entry, and the job-groups key, are never touched: they come out as they went in.

  1. Full run. Plan a full run when any of these holds:

    • --force-full;
    • the branch is the default branch, or there is a tag;
    • the trigger type is schedule;
    • the head commit asks for one;
    • there is no base, or no usable map;
    • a changed path (old or new) matches --full-run-paths;
    • W has a when or unless that cannot be evaluated (see below). When when/unless can be evaluated and is false for this pipeline (workflow_runs in the plan report), the workflow is left untouched (no gate, no pruning) and every job is reported as skipped. 1b. Workflow when/unless. After the full-run checks above, evaluate W’s when and unless when every value they use is known: literal booleans; << pipeline.parameters.NAME >>; logic statements and, or, not, equal and matches; and the string expression form (pipeline.git.branch == "main", !=, and/or/not, starts-with). Known pipeline values come from --branch, --tag, --trigger-type and --parameters. If evaluation succeeds and the workflow would not run, stop (step 1, last bullet). If any subexpression is unknown or unsupported, treat it like step 1 (full run). If it would run, continue.

  2. Changes. Run git diff --name-status -M -z <base> <head>.

    • Renames count as the old path deleted plus the new path added.
    • Paths that match --ignore-paths are dropped before step 3.

  3. Direct selection. For each entry J of W (its effective name is name: if set, else the job reference). An entry that does not run on this branch or tag (step 5) is never selected, whatever else holds, so it never seeds step 4:

    • approval and no-op entries are decided by the closure in step 4, and so are release entries (by the rule there). None has a trace, so none has inputs of its own, and --mandatory does not force them. The exception is a gatekeeper: a no-op entry that no entry requires, that waits for success only, and that runs on this branch or tag (step 5). It is kept, with the reason “kept: a no-op gatekeeper”, whatever else is selected. It selects nothing: it is not part of the closure;
    • a job group entry runs, with the reason “job group: runs as one unit, as v0.1 does not look inside it” (and it is not traced, step 8);
    • a matrix entry runs;
    • a mandatory job runs. If step 5 says it does not run here, the planner leaves it out and records a warning; it does not force a job to run;
    • a job whose extra inputs match a changed path runs;
    • a job with no map entry, or an incomplete one, runs;
    • a job that read a changed file runs;
    • for an added or deleted path P, J runs if J listed the parent directory of P. It also runs if J listed any ancestor directory whose direct child on P’s path is a directory that is new at the head or gone from the base (use git ls-tree at the base and the head);
    • otherwise J is skipped, with the reason “inputs unchanged”.

  4. Closure.

    • Every requires ancestor of a selected job is selected, approvals and no-op jobs included, except an ancestor that does not run (step 5). CircleCI ignores a requirement on such a job, and step 7 drops it. So an approval, or a no-op job that some entry requires, is skipped when no selected job requires it, with the reason “no selected job requires this approval” (or “no-op job”).
    • A release entry is selected when any job it requires is selected (“tracks the release of X”); its other requirements are selected like those of any selected job. Otherwise it is skipped: “none of the jobs it requires is selected”.
    • Producers are local jobs with persist_to_workspace; consumers are local jobs with attach_workspace. Steps in a local command, and in the entry’s own pre-steps and post-steps, count. Orb jobs and job groups count as both.
    • When a selected producer K has a consumer J downstream of it, J is selected.
    • Repeat both rules until nothing changes.

  5. Will it run? Evaluate filters for the current branch or tag:

    • CircleCI semantics: string or list, and /regex/ is a full match;
    • jobs do not run on tags without a matching tags.only;
    • expression (string) filters are unknown; they are reported;
    • this is CircleCI’s own rule (configuration reference, requires): a requirement on a job that does not run is ignored, but a job whose requirements are all filtered out does not run either. So a job runs only if its own filters allow it and, when it has requirements, at least one of them runs, all the way up the graph. A job with one filtered-out requirement and one that runs still runs, after the one that runs;
    • a requirement on a job status other than success (- build: failed), or on a name that no entry answers to, makes the job unknown, unless its own filters already say it does not run.

  6. Gate. Add the job smarter-gate:

    • its definition is smarter-gate: {type: no-op}, with no executor and no steps, so it costs no credits. This is CircleCI’s documented gatekeeper pattern for one required status check. It needs a workflow entry like any job, and it fails only if a job it requires fails;
    • its workflow entry requires every selected job that will certainly run (step 5 says yes), except approvals, no-op jobs (they run no steps, so they fail only with the jobs they require, which the gate waits for) and jobs downstream of an approval (an approval that step 5 says does not run is not there to wait for). A selected job that is unknown is left out, with a warning that names it: a job whose filters cannot be evaluated, or smarter-gate does not wait for X: it requires a job status other than success (a job that waits for a failure may never run, and the gate would wait for it for ever);
    • if nothing else is selected, W contains only the gate.

  7. Emit.

    • Select mode: remove the skipped entries from W. From the entries that stay, drop a requires name only when it names a removed job that does not run (step 5): CircleCI ignores it, so the meaning is the same. Never drop the last name of a list, and never a name that is a job that runs: that could change what runs. If the plan would, it is an internal error: a full run.
    • A gatekeeper (step 3) stays in select mode, and its requires is cut to the entries that stay: every name of an entry that is removed goes, whether that entry would run or not, and the items that stay keep their form. If none stays, it requires the gate, so that it never passes before the selected jobs have. A project that makes its gatekeeper (say all-tests-passed) the required status check keeps one that reports. A gatekeeper that does not run on this branch (all it requires is filtered out) is left out like any entry that does not run.
    • Shadow mode: keep every entry. The report still shows what select mode would have skipped.
    • Every other part of the config keeps its meaning: other workflows, jobs, orbs, comments and key order.
    • Never add pipeline parameters. Emit literals only.

  8. Trace (full runs on the default branch, when --trace resolves to on) — superseded by ADR 8; removed in v0.3:

    1. On every entry of W that is a local Linux job (docker, or machine with a Linux image), append post-steps. An approval, a no-op job, a release job, a job group and a matrix entry get none. Orb jobs are included only with --trace-orb-jobs; without it, an orb entry gets no pre-steps and no post-steps. A pre-steps or post-steps key with no value is an empty list. An entry whose pre-steps or post-steps is not a list gets no trace, with a warning: the others are traced, and since it has no map entry, later plans always run it.
      • a run step named smarter: collect trace, with when: always, shell: /bin/sh, and as its command the embedded collect-trace.sh;
      • persist_to_workspace with root /tmp/smarter and paths [traces].
    2. If the spike (W3) shows that checkout itself reads files, also insert a step right after the first checkout of the job: a top-level step, or right after a local command invocation whose definition contains checkout (including nested commands, up to a depth limit). For checkout: {path: X}, the reset and collect steps get CIRCLE_WORKING_DIRECTORY set to that path. The planner cannot reach the checkout inside an orb job, so with --trace-orb-jobs an orb entry gets pre-steps [checkout, <that reset step>] instead: it checks out first, then resets, and the orb job’s own checkout follows. Jobs with no checkout are not traced. The plan report lists every workflow job in trace_coverage, with a reason when it is not traced (unknown executor, no checkout, job group, matrix, orb without --trace-orb-jobs, and so on).
    3. Add the job smarter-impact-map. It requires every traced entry that is not downstream of an approval. Its steps:
      1. write .smarter-version (the planner’s own version, as a literal);
      2. restore_cache with key smarter-bin-v1-{{ checksum ".smarter-version" }}-{{ arch }};
      3. attach_workspace at /tmp/smarter;
      4. map build;
      5. write .smarter-key ($CIRCLE_SHA1);
      6. save_cache with key <--map-key-prefix>-{{ checksum ".smarter-key" }} (by default smarter-impact-v1-{{ checksum ".smarter-key" }}) for /tmp/smarter/impact-map.json.gz;
      7. store_artifacts.

  9. Guardrails (when --policy-bundle is set):

    1. policy.Check the emitted config.
    2. For a hard violation carrying [smarter:require-job=NAME], force NAME and plan again (at most 3 rounds). Forcing selects the job; it cannot make a job run that step 5 says does not run here, so the violation stays and step 3 applies.
    3. If hard violations are left, plan a full run and check again.
    4. If that still fails, exit 3.
    5. Soft violations go into the report as warnings.

Guardrail bundle (policies/)

  • package org, using CircleCI’s policy conventions (policy_name, enable_hard) and data.circleci.config helpers where they fit.
  • The settings are constants at the top of the file, for projects to edit.
  • Rules:
    1. Required jobs (security-scan by default) are present in every workflow of a non-setup config. The message carries the repair code.
    2. Restricted contexts (e.g. deploy): allowed only on listed jobs, only on listed branches or on tags, and only downstream of an approval job (type: approval on the entry, or in the job’s definition).
    3. Resource classes come from an allowlist. Check the source jobs, and _compiled_ when it is present. A no-op job has no executor, so it is not checked.
    4. Registry orbs are pinned to an exact x.y.z.
    5. URL orbs carry a 40-hex commit SHA.
    6. A continuation config does not declare setup: true.
  • Tests: Rego _test.rego files plus Go fixture tests through internal/policy. Locally there is no _compiled_, so rules must cope with it being absent.

The orb and the dogfood pipeline

  • orb/src/ (orb-tools tree, packed to one file):
    • command install (source: release|build; build runs go build from the current checkout and saves the smarter-bin-v1-… cache);
    • command collect-trace;
    • job plan, with parameters mirroring the plan flags. It runs: checkout, install, base → .smarter-key, restore the map cache (exact key, then the <map-key-prefix>- prefix, smarter-impact-v1- by default), plan, store the report, continue.
  • .circleci/config.yml: setup, with an inline plan job that builds from source (the orb is not published yet).
  • .circleci/continue.yml: this repo’s own full pipeline, which includes:
    • Go tests and lint;
    • policy tests;
    • shellcheck and collector tests;
    • orb validation;
    • the docs site build (docs-site-build), which reads only the docs and the site sources, and the publication of the site from main (docs-site-publish, in the workflow docs-site);
    • security-scan (mandatory; govulncheck);
    • a build → e2e pair over a workspace;
    • a tag-only signed binary release after hold-release, with dev and production orb publish jobs.

Tests and gates (before any merge to main)

  • gofmt -l is empty, and go vet ./... and go test ./... pass.
  • Golden tests for the planner scenarios in examples/monorepo/:
    • docs-only;
    • one service;
    • a shared library;
    • an added file in a listed directory;
    • a .circleci change;
    • no map;
    • a mandatory job missing and then repaired.
  • Robustness cases cover each job type (approval set in the definition, no-op, release, job group, serial-group). Every plan has a no-op gate and no structural problem that layout check would report and the input did not have.
  • The catalog of the example (examples/monorepo/catalog.json) is a golden file, refreshed with go test ./examples/monorepo -update like the scenarios.
  • Every config the planner generates validates with circleci config validate when the CLI is present. Set REQUIRE_CIRCLECI_CLI=1 in CI so that a missing CLI fails, not skips.
  • Collector tests run in a temp git repo. With REQUIRE_ATIME=1, a filesystem without atime support fails the test.
  • The continuation client is tested against httptest, and the test asserts the key never appears in the output.

item.title: 2. Skip a job only when the impact map proves the change cannot reach it
item.description:
Date: 2026-11-13. Status: accepted (open for review).

Context

A skipped job that would have failed (a miss) costs more than an extra job that passes. Path filters miss when their globs drift from what jobs really read. Learned models miss when history is thin. GitHub branch protection also waits forever on a required check whose job was skipped.

Decision

  1. Every job runs unless the planner can show that the change touches none of its inputs:
    • no changed file is among the files the impact map lists for the job;
    • no added or deleted file sits in a directory the job lists.
  2. These always run:
    • jobs with no map entry, an incomplete entry, or inputs that fail the skip proof in ADR 8;
    • mandatory jobs;
    • every ancestor (requires) of a selected job, approvals included.
  3. A full run happens:
    • on the default branch and on tags;
    • for scheduled pipelines;
    • when the change touches the pipeline definition (.circleci/** by default);
    • when there is no impact map, the diff base cannot be found, or the planner hits any error;
    • when the head commit asks for one.
  4. Every decision layer added later (history, models) can only add jobs.
  5. Every workflow the planner prunes ends in one gate job, smarter-gate, which requires every selected job that will run. It is a no-op job (type: no-op), so it costs no credits. So the workflow always exists and its check always reports:
    • GitHub App projects report one check per workflow, and branch protection requires that check;
    • with per-job statuses, branch protection requires the gate alone.

Consequences

  • Savings come from skipping the parts of the job graph a change cannot reach, such as other services in a monorepo. Shared early jobs, like a repo-wide lint, still run.
  • It assumes a job’s behaviour depends on the repo files it reads. Inputs from outside the repo (the network, the time, secrets, upstream images) are covered by the full run on the default branch, by mandatory jobs, and by extra inputs a project declares by hand.
  • A project may already use a no-op job that nothing requires as its one required status check (a gatekeeper, such as all-tests-passed). The planner always keeps it, and cuts what it waits for to the jobs that stay, or to the gate, so its check always reports and never passes early.
  • A job that does not run on the branch (its own filters leave it out, or all the jobs it requires are left out) is never selected, even when it is mandatory. The planner does not edit the project’s filters or requirements to force a job. It leaves such a job out, and a mandatory one gets a warning. It drops a requires name only when it names a job that does not run, which CircleCI ignores anyway.
  • Skipping a job on confidence alone, without proof, is out of scope until shadow-mode data shows recall of at least 99% for that job.

item.title: Analyze
item.description:
circleci-smarter analyze infers which repository paths can reach each job. v0.3 uses this map instead of trace injection.

What it reads

Static signals from the config and checkout: run commands and scripts they invoke, Node and Python manifests, Dockerfile COPY, working_directory, orb parameters such as app-dir, cache-key checksum files, workspace flow, path-filtering mappings, and Go imports (go/parser, including tests; module, go.work, replace, //go:embed, and vendor/).

AI classifier

With --ai auto (default), analyze calls Anthropic when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is set. Modes: on (failure stops the run), off (static and history only), dry-run (writes request JSON under <report-dir>/ai-requests/ without sending).

The prompt sends job definitions, a repo tree, and trimmed file text within --ai-max-input-tokens (default 90k). Structured JSON is enforced with output_config.format.

Never sent: paths matching .env*, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa*, credential/secret filenames, .npmrc, .pypirc, .netrc, binaries, or files over 256 KiB (listed in the tree only).

Learned layer

--learned-out writes version-1 JSON: per job job_hash, optional AI inputs with confidence, and history corrections (paths added when a non-flaky failure’s changed files were outside the map). --learned merges corrections forward and drops paths that no longer exist. AI may mark a job complete only when job_hash matches and confidence >= --min-confidence.

Report

--report and --report-json list each job’s completeness, why it is incomplete, and inputs grouped by config signal. Totals include AI call counts, token use, and estimated cost (Haiku 5.5 tier; prices as of 2026-10).

Run locally

Paths such as --config and --history are relative to --repo (the repository root you are analyzing). To analyze the demo config from this repository, run from the repo root:

circleci-smarter analyze --repo . --config examples/demo/.circleci/continue.yml --workflow demo --ai off
circleci-smarter analyze --repo . --ai off --report analyze-report.md

Map output defaults to smarter-map.json in the current working directory (where you run the command).

Developers can add recall/precision against a reference map with --truth FILE (omitted from routine operator docs).

The weekly learn job runs analyze with AI and history, writes the learned layer, and backtests recall. plan merges that layer on every pipeline without calling the API.

item.title: Compose eval
item.description:
Can an agent with the workflow composer skill assemble CircleCI jobs into a correct workflow? Each case gives it the demo’s job definitions (jobs.yml, the demo’s continue.yml without its workflows) and a goal. It answers with a complete config: the jobs as given, plus the workflows: it composed.

check.sh then judges each answer, with no model involved:

  1. circleci config validate;
  2. circleci-smarter layout check, with mandatory security-scan and restricted context deploy;
  3. circleci-smarter policy check against policies/;
  4. the case’s own assertions (which jobs must be in it, and in what order).
Case Goal
1 compose the full workflow for main and branches, from scratch
2 compose the smallest correct workflow for a set of selected jobs
3 repair a broken layout (case-3-broken.yml) from the checker’s findings

The results of the first run are in the validation page, and the answers are in answers/.

item.title: Demo monorepo
item.description:
A small polyglot monorepo that runs on Smarter Workflows. Every job does real but fast work, so you can watch the planner pick jobs from a change.

services/api Go, with a handler and a test
services/web Node, tested with node:test
services/worker Python, tested with unittest
libs/proto schema.json, read by the api and the web tests
docs/ Markdown, checked for titles and links
infra/ Terraform files, checked for their shape
scripts/ what the lint, docs, infra, security and e2e jobs run

The pipeline

.circleci/config.yml is the setup config. It builds the planner from this repository, plans .circleci/continue.yml (workflow demo) and continues the pipeline with the result.

Job Reads
lint the source of the three services and the schema, not docs
api-test the api and the schema
web-test the web service and the schema
web-bundle the web service (a job from the circleci/node orb)
worker-test a matrix over two Python versions, which always runs
docs-check docs/
infra-validate infra/
security-scan everything; it is mandatory, so it always runs
build, e2e the api; e2e attaches the binary that build persists
hold-deploy, deploy main only, after a person approves

On main every job runs, and its file reads become the impact map. On a branch only the jobs the change can reach run, plus smarter-gate.

The demo keeps its impact map under its own cache key prefix, smarter-demo-impact-v1, because the repository’s own pipeline shares the project cache. The scenarios in scripts/e2e/scenarios-demo.tsv check what runs for each kind of change, and Validation lists the results.

item.title: Glossary
item.description:
The words this project uses, and what each one means. There are no implementation details here. For those, see the spec and the decisions.

Change
The set of files a branch changes, compared with the commit it branched from on the default branch.
Planner
The step in the setup workflow that decides, for one change, which jobs of the pipeline run.
Plan
What the planner decides for one pipeline: the jobs that run, the jobs that are skipped and the reason for each, and the continuation config that carries this out.
Full run
A pipeline that runs every job. The default branch, scheduled pipelines, changes to the pipeline definition, and any case the planner is unsure about all get a full run.
Impact map
For each job, the repo files and directories the planner treats as its inputs. circleci-smarter analyze builds it from the continuation config and the repository. Branches use the map to see which jobs a change can affect.
Inputs (of a job)
The files and directories listed for a job in the impact map. Exact files match only that path; each input dir covers every path under it recursively; . is the repository root and covers the whole tree. Any change status uses the same rule. A job whose inputs a change does not touch is a candidate to skip.
Input dir
A directory entry in a job’s impact map. It includes every file and subdirectory under that path, not only direct children.
Shadow mode
The planner makes and reports a plan, but every job still runs. Shadow mode measures what select mode would save, and what it would miss.
Select mode
The planner runs only the jobs its plan selects.
Compose mode
A later mode: an agent builds jobs and workflows from approved building blocks, within the guardrails.
Mandatory job
A job that runs in every pipeline, whatever the change, such as a security scan.
Gate job
The last job of the workflow, which waits for every selected job. It always runs, so a branch protection rule can require it alone, even when other jobs are skipped. It is a no-op job: no executor, no steps, no credits.
No-op job
A job defined with type: no-op. It runs nothing and costs no credits. It succeeds when the jobs it requires succeed.
Gatekeeper
A no-op job that no other job requires, which a project uses as its one required status check (for example all-tests-passed). Select mode always keeps it, and cuts what it waits for to the jobs that stay.
Layout
How the jobs of one workflow wait for each other (requires, approvals, filters), as opposed to what each job does. layout check reports what is wrong with it.
Guardrail
A config policy that every generated config must pass. Examples: mandatory jobs, contexts allowed only on certain jobs and branches, an approval before a deploy.
Pre-flight
The planner’s own check of its config against the guardrails, before it continues the pipeline.
Repair
A change the planner makes to its plan so that it passes a guardrail, such as adding a missing mandatory job. A failure it cannot repair turns the plan into a full run.
Miss
A job the plan skipped (or, in shadow mode, would have skipped) that would have failed.
Savings
The credits and minutes that skipped jobs did not spend.
Catalog
The jobs, commands, executors and orbs the planner may pick from. In select mode, the catalog is the project’s own pipeline config.
Analyze
The circleci-smarter analyze command that infers per-job repo inputs from CircleCI config and checkout sources, optionally aided by history and an AI classifier.
Job hash
A stable SHA-256 of a job’s resolved config (body, commands, executors, pinned orbs, and workflow entry parameters). Used to reuse AI output safely in the learned layer.
Learned layer
A versioned cache of costly analyze output: AI mappings and history corrections keyed by job name and job hash.
AI classifier
The optional Anthropic call that suggests extra paths per job, constrained by structured JSON output and confidence.
Confidence
The model’s 0–1 self-rating for a job’s inferred inputs. Analyze treats a job as complete from AI only when confidence meets --min-confidence and the job hash matches.
Learn
The circleci-smarter learn command that fetches pipeline history, refreshes the learned layer with AI and corrections, and reports recall and projected savings.
AI review
An optional plan-time model call that may add skipped jobs (never remove them) when a pipeline would skip work; failures leave the deterministic plan unchanged.
